content: Dimples are visible indentations on the skin that occur due to the underlying structure of the flesh. They typically appear on some individuals' cheeks when they smile. These dimples are inherited genetically and are considered a dominant trait. It is relatively common for individuals with dimples to have them on both cheeks. However, a less common variation is the presence of a single dimple, which appears on only one side of the face. From an anatomical perspective, dimples are thought to result from variations in the structure of the zygomaticus major muscle, a facial muscle. Specifically, the presence of a bifid, or double, zygomaticus major muscle may explain the formation of cheek dimples. This bifid muscle variation originates as a single structure from the zygomatic bone. As it extends forward (anteriorly), it divides into two separate bundles. The superior bundle inserts into the typical position above the corner of the mouth, while the inferior bundle inserts below the corner of the mouth. Dimples are often regarded as an attractive feature in certain cultures. They are commonly observed in babies, but these dimples may fade or become less noticeable over time as the facial muscles lengthen with age. For this reason, dimples are frequently associated with youthfulness.
